reuse.capability: Six-plane repository preservation: capture remote base, remote PR head, local commits, index, tracked worktree and untracked/ignored inventory into a sealed capsule that can be restore-tested in a clean room before any risky operation.

candidates.name: git bundle --all
candidates.platform_fit: native, already used in this workspace
candidates.probe: PROBED 2026-08-17: init repo, stage a change, leave an unstaged change, add an untracked file, bundle --all, clone. Result — committed content YES; index change NO; unstaged worktree change NO; untracked file NO. Covers plane C only of six. This is the exact gap that lost the cleaned opencode.jsonc during the 2026-08-09 root pass.

candidates.name: git stash -u
candidates.probe: PROBED 2026-08-17: created a real merge conflict, staged a resolution, ran git stash -u. Result — MERGE_HEAD destroyed, staged resolution destroyed, stash pop did not restore either. Reproduces the failure that forced a full redo of the pr/38 reconciliation on the same day. Actively unsafe mid-operation; not a preservation mechanism.

candidates.name: restic / borgbackup
candidates.platform_fit: general file-tree backup; no git-plane semantics
candidates.probe: not_probed: backs up file trees, has no concept of index vs worktree vs remote ref, and cannot express 'restore-tested in a clean room against an exact remote SHA'. Would preserve bytes without preserving the six-plane distinction that is the whole point.

candidates.name: BagIt (RFC 8493)
candidates.probe: not_probed: genuinely relevant for the sealed-capsule half (payload manifest with checksums) and worth revisiting if the capsule format is ever externalised. Does not address capture or clean-room restore-test, which is where the risk lives.

candidates.name: OCFL
candidates.platform_fit: versioned object storage for preservation repositories
candidates.probe: not_probed: designed for long-term archival object storage, not point-in-time operational snapshots of a live working tree. Heavier than the problem.

candidates.name: in-toto attestations
candidates.probe: not_probed: attests that a step ran with given materials/products; it does not capture or restore repository state. Complementary to, not a substitute for, capture. Already named in RESEARCH-REGISTER as the preferred provenance format over anything bespoke.

reuse.irreducible_delta: No candidate captures planes D (index), E (tracked worktree) and F (untracked/ignored) alongside C (commits) as one restore-testable unit anchored to an exact remote SHA. git bundle covers C only (probed); git stash is destructive mid-merge (probed); restic/borg preserve bytes without git-plane semantics; BagIt/OCFL address packaging and archival storage, not capture or clean-room verification; in-toto attests steps rather than state. The irreducible delta is the six-plane contract plus fail-closed restore-testing — 'if preservation cannot be proved, salvage stops'. BagIt remains the strongest partial and should be reconsidered if the capsule format is ever published beyond this workspace.
